items.text: Across 23 school clinics, will a lean redesign of the SDF pathway raise the proportion of children with an active cavity at screening who receive SDF soon after screening from about 41 percent to at least 60 percent by the end of the spring term 2027, in every home-language group?
items.population: Children with at least one active cavity at a school screening visit
items.intervention: Redesigned pathway: combined consent with a staining photograph, need-ordered call list, staining leaflet
items.outcome: Proportion receiving SDF soon after screening, by home language

items.text: How do parents, teachers and dental therapists experience the redesigned pathway, and what makes SDF acceptable or unacceptable to families, including families with limited English?
items.population: Parents of screened children, class teachers, school office staff and dental therapists
items.intervention: Experience of the redesigned SDF pathway
items.outcome: Views on consent, staining, disruption and fairness
items.time: After the first and third test cycles
items.setting: Six of the 23 schools chosen for variation in home language

finer: Both questions are feasible within existing records, one analyst day a week and approved conversations; interesting to the unit and the school board; novel locally; ethical under PHU-REC-2026-22; relevant because uptake is low and some families may be left behind.
summary: A QI aim for the measurement strand and a SPIDER question for the conversation strand, kept separate.
